item.title: PTZ Industry Problem Map & Edge AI Computing
item.description: The security department at our campus swapped out three batches of PTZ cameras last year. The maintenance team’s fault list kept cycling through the same few items: faces in the lobby look like silhouettes under strong backlit daylight, night shots are wall-to-wall noise at low light, IR illumination attracts swarms of insects, and we get dropouts during cold snaps. Any one of these looks like “this camera is bad,” but what’s actually happening is that the PTZ product category is hitting boundaries in three layers: optical imaging, engineering deployment, and collaborative intelligence.

item.title: YOLO Model Export Explained: 22 Formats, Parameters, and How to Choose
item.description: When I wrote “YOLO Deployment” in May 2026, the official Ultralytics export table had 17 rows. By September, when this post came together, it had grown to 22 — every new row is an NPU vendor pipeline: ExecuTorch, Axelera, DEEPX, Hailo, Huawei Ascend, Apple Core AI, and the like. The direction of growth is clear: training frameworks and inference hardware are drifting apart. PyTorch handles training, each deployment target runs its own runtime, and export is the only bridge between the two.

item.title: RuView: WiFi-Based Pose Estimation and Contactless Vital Signs
item.description:
The previous post covered ESPectre, which uses WiFi CSI to answer “is anyone moving in the room?” RuView wants more: not just motion, but 17 body keypoints, breathing rate, heart rate, and through-wall sensing, all decoded from the same signals. It is written in Rust by ruvnet (the author of claude-flow), MIT-licensed, and with 92,000+ stars as of September 2026 it is the hottest open-source project in this space.

The conclusion first, so you don’t over-expect: this is a beta-stage research platform. The gap between the pose model’s benchmark-dataset score and its on-device score is large, and APIs and firmware are still moving. It still deserves a serious write-up for two reasons. First, the pipeline is a textbook-grade WiFi-sensing architecture — from multi-band fusion to vital-sign extraction, every stage carries something transferable to other sensing problems. Second, the project labels “which numbers are real and which are scaffolding” in an explicit three-tier maturity table — that level of honest self-labeling is rare in open-source AI projects.
